newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo hits new peak after results.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo hits new peak after results.

text.p: Shares in British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc advanced to a record high on Thursday after the group posted its 1996 results and announced a new drilling project.
At 0912 GMT, the shares were up 9p to 1467-1/2, having climbed as high as 1480 initially.

The UK oil exploration group, whose shares have soared some 80 percent since the start of the year largely on bid speculation, said its pre-tax profits rose to 19.51 million in the year ended December 31, 1996.
The group also said it would participate in around 30 exploration and appraisal wells this year nFLLF3K03M.
"The market is up purely on the figures," said one market maker.
But Credit Lyonnais Laing analyst Jurjen Lunshof said the company's results fell a bit short of his expectations.
Lunshof, who maintained his "sell" recommendation on the stock, said the company was "over-hyped and over-valued."
"I'm not denying that management has done a very good job ... but I don't think anyone is going to bid for a company with such a heavy premium," he said.
